saints.name: Sts. Crispin and Crispinian
saints.title: Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: Two brothers who preached the Gospel by day and made shoes by night, martyred at Soissons…
biography: According to their ancient legend, Crispin and Crispinian were brothers, perhaps of noble Roman birth, who came to Gaul to spread the Christian faith. Settling at Soissons, they supported themselves and gave to the poor by working as shoemakers, preaching to those who came to them.

During the persecution under the emperor Diocletian they were arrested, tortured, and put to death about the year 286. They became the beloved patrons of shoemakers, cobblers, and leatherworkers, and their feast, “Saint Crispin's Day,” long held a place in popular memory.
saints.knownFor: Working as shoemakers while preaching the Gospel.
